title: Maritime NDT & Class Audit Support | Groton, Connecticut
description: NDT audit prep for Groton-area submarine suppliers and gauging firms: NAVSEA flow-down, trainee records, procedures and class audits. Talk to a Level III.
h1: Maritime NDT Consulting & Class Audit Support in Groton
html:
Groton's shipyard is hiring and buying at a pace the region has not seen in decades, and every new supplier and NDT subcontractor that joins the submarine supply chain has to show that its inspection program can stand up to review. This page is for those firms: fabricators, machine shops, foundries and NDT companies in southeastern Connecticut and across New England, plus the smaller group of gauging firms that serve commercial vessels on Long Island Sound. Acting as your outside ASNT NDT Level III, Atlantis NDT helps get the written practice, procedures and records ready, and to rehearse the audit with you. Tell us who is auditing you and when, and we will set out a plan.

Where submarines learned to be welded

Electric Boat's own history puts weld inspection at the start of Groton's story. In 1934 the company delivered Cuttlefish, which it describes as the first submarine built in Groton for the Navy and the first welded submarine. Groton had built its first hull a decade earlier, on an order from Peru. Through the Second World War the company produced 74 submarines, and in 1997 it delivered Louisiana, the eighteenth and last Trident ballistic-missile boat.

Today General Dynamics Electric Boat designs and builds Virginia-class attack submarines and is the prime contractor for the Columbia-class ballistic-missile submarine program. Its shipyard is in Groton, its hull fabrication and outfitting facility is at Quonset Point in North Kingstown, Rhode Island, and its engineering offices are across the Thames in New London. The company also maintains and modernizes submarines across the fleet. The Quonset Point site dates from 1973, and when the first hull section of the lead Virginia-class boat reached Groton in 2000, it showed how the work is split: large sections are built at one site and joined at the other. Naval Submarine Base New London, despite its name, also sits on the Groton side of the river.

The 2026 award and what it does to the supply chain

On July 29, 2026, the Defense Department announced a multibillion-dollar set of contracts for Electric Boat to build nine more Virginia-class and five more Columbia-class submarines, with the work spread between Groton and other US locations. Local reporting quoted the company's plan to hire about 8,000 people by the end of 2026 and roughly the same number in 2027, and noted that Quonset Point, which builds mid-body sections for both classes, will receive new fixturing, buildings and assembly halls.

Numbers like that do not stay inside the shipyard gate. They pull in second- and third-tier suppliers that have never built for submarines, and they push existing suppliers to add people quickly. Both trends land on NDT. A new supplier arrives with an inspection program written for aerospace, power generation or general fabrication. An established supplier hires trainees faster than it can document their training and experience. In both cases the first serious test of the program is an audit, and the auditor works from Navy requirements.

Who looks at a submarine supplier's NDT

Suppliers in this region generally deal with three layers of oversight, and each one reads the same documents for slightly different reasons.

  • The prime's supplier quality organization decides whether you may supply at all. It reviews your quality system, samples your NDT program against the requirements in its purchase orders, and often comes back after your first deliveries to see whether practice matches paper.
  • The Navy's Supervisor of Shipbuilding is the government inspector for Navy contracts placed with privately owned yards such as Electric Boat. Its staff can review the NDT behind any product delivered under the contract, including yours.
  • Submarine safety requirements add a further layer for material and work that falls inside the boundary the Navy's submarine safety program controls. Expect stricter traceability and objective quality evidence requirements on those items, flowed down through the purchase order. The order, not the supplier, defines which items are affected.

Behind all three sits NAVSEA Technical Publication T9074-AS-GIB-010/271, which tells an activity how to qualify its NDT people, procedures and equipment for RT, MT, PT, UT, ET and VT; the accept and reject limits themselves are printed on the drawing or written into the order. Submarine work follows NAVSEA requirements, not classification society rules. Our T9074 compliance page and NAVSEA shipyard requirements guide explain the publication in depth.

Bringing an NDT program over from another industry

Many of the firms now approaching Electric Boat's supply chain already run competent NDT programs. The trouble is that those programs were written for someone else's rules. Some parts carry over intact; others need real rework.

Part of the programUsually carries overUsually needs rework for Navy-flowed work
Written practiceStructure, levels, method coverage, responsibility statementsTreating SNT-TC-1A as mandatory minimums, three-year recertification by examination, annual surveillance, the Navy near-vision line
Personnel certificationTraining records and examinations that already meet the hours and contentCertifications renewed without examination, and any certificate accepted from a former employer
ProceduresTechnical content for the method and product formExaminer approval and qualification on specimens with known discontinuities in your own shop
Equipment controlCalibration intervals and certificatesRecords that tie each inspection to a specific serial-numbered instrument and reference standard
RecordsBasic report contentRetention and retrieval to the customer's requirements, and links from each report to procedure revision and inspector certification

The conversion usually takes less effort than suppliers fear, as long as it is done before the audit rather than in reply to it. Our written practice development service handles the rewrite, and procedure qualification and demonstration covers proving each procedure on representative specimens.

Hiring fast without breaking the certification trail

A supplier adding NDT trainees at Groton's current pace faces a records problem before it faces a skills problem. Every trainee needs documented classroom training, documented on-the-job experience under a certified inspector, examinations and a vision test before certification, and every one of those needs a date and a signature. When hiring outruns the paperwork, auditors find experience logs filled in after the fact, training hours that do not add up, and examinations graded by the same person who wrote them without anyone checking.

We help suppliers set up the training side as a system rather than a scramble. That means a written practice that states the hours and examinations for each method and level, templates for logging supervised experience as it happens, an examination bank your Level III maintains, and a calendar that flags recertification and surveillance before they lapse. Our pages on SNT-TC-1A training program setup and NDT experience logs describe the pieces, and the SNT-TC-1A hours planner helps estimate how long a trainee needs before certification. Remember that Navy-flowed work tightens several of those requirements, so the plan has to start from the stricter rule.

Certificates that quietly expire are the most frequent single finding. Suppliers growing quickly can use our certificate tracking app or read our guide to stopping expired technician certifications.

Retaining records and closing findings

Submarines stay in service for decades, and the records behind their parts are expected to last as long as the customer requires. A supplier that keeps inspection reports in a shared drive with no retention rule, or that cannot find the certification that was valid on the day of an inspection three years ago, will struggle in any audit that samples old work. Retention periods and formats come from your purchase orders and the publications they invoke; our T9074 records retention page covers what to look for.

When findings do come, the response matters as much as the fix. Auditors want to see the cause, the correction to the specific item, the action that stops it recurring, and evidence for each. A corrective action that says "retrained staff" without a dated training record will be reopened. Our T9074 corrective actions page sets out what a closed finding needs to contain.

What sits outside Atlantis's scope

Every submarine built in Groton is nuclear-powered. Work on the propulsion plant, and the quality assurance regime around it, are outside Atlantis's scope, and we say so before an engagement starts. We support suppliers on non-nuclear hull structure, tanks, piping, foundations, castings and outfitting.

We also do not perform radiography in the United States. If your parts need RT, a licensed radiography provider performs it; our Level III can review that provider's procedure, images and personnel qualification for your subcontractor file. Welding procedures and welder qualification stay with your welding engineer, since we do not write or qualify welding procedures.

Commercial vessels and class audits on the Connecticut coast

Groton's economy is dominated by submarines, but commercial and passenger vessels operating on Long Island Sound and calling at New England ports still need class surveys, and some of those surveys rely on thickness measurement. If a surveyor is going to credit those readings toward class, UR Z17 says the firm doing the gauging must be approved by the society that classes the vessel, and a thickness measurement approval comes up for renewal at least once every three years. Our IACS service supplier approval guide explains the document review, office audit and witnessed demonstration involved.

On our own status: for thickness measurement, our company is currently in the process of obtaining UR Z17 approval from ABS, Lloyd's Register and DNV, and none of the three has granted it yet. That keeps our maritime role advisory for now. We can prepare a gauging firm for its class audit, but we cannot provide class-credited readings until a society certifies us.

How an engagement runs with a Groton-area supplier

Atlantis has no office in New England. Its founder, Anoop Rayavarapu, is certified by ASNT as an NDT Level III in the UT, RT, MT, PT and VT methods and has spent more than 11 years in international field work; he leads the Level III side of each engagement. Document work happens remotely, and we travel to your shop when the job needs someone on the floor.

  • First conversation: you share the purchase order requirements, the prime's supplier quality manual or audit notice, and your current written practice.
  • Gap register: we produce a single list of gaps between your program and the requirements, ranked by how likely each one is to become a finding.
  • Rebuild: we draft the written practice, procedures, examination materials and record templates for approval by your management and your Level III or Examiner.
  • Prove and rehearse: our Level III witnesses each procedure qualification, then audits your facility the way the prime's team will.
  • After the audit: we help you write corrective actions that close.

Responsibility stays where the rules put it. Your company signs the certifications and keeps the files; approval as a supplier is the prime's call; compliance with the publication is judged by the Navy's inspector. Atlantis gets you ready for each of those judgments without taking any of them over.

What to send us

  • The quality clauses from your purchase orders, the specifications they cite, or the prime's audit letter.
  • Your current written practice and the name of the Level III or Examiner who signs it.
  • Your NDT procedures and any qualification records.
  • A sample of personnel files, especially recent hires and trainees.
  • Your equipment list with calibration status and a few recent reports.
  • Any findings from previous customer audits.

We reply within one business day. For technician development, see maritime NDT training in Groton and the Groton NDT training page.

Groton supplier readiness checklist

  1. Confirm which of your orders invoke NAVSEA NDT requirements and which items fall inside the submarine safety boundary.
  2. Check that your written practice states the Navy rules where your orders call for them.
  3. Make sure every procedure used on submarine work has Examiner approval and a qualification record from your shop.
  4. Audit trainee files for dated training, supervised experience, examinations and vision tests.
  5. Recertify inspectors who joined with certifications from another employer.
  6. Set a retention rule for inspection records that matches your orders, and test that you can retrieve old reports.
  7. Review radiography and other NDT subcontractor files before the auditor asks.
  8. Close every open corrective action with evidence.

For the national overview, see maritime NDT audit support and our shipbuilding audit support page. Other New England yards have their own pages for Bath, Maine, Portsmouth, New Hampshire and New Haven, and statewide Level III work is on the Connecticut consulting page and our Groton consulting page. For Hampton Roads, where the Virginia-class teaming partner builds, see Newport News.

faq.q: Does submarine work for Electric Boat follow classification society rules?
faq.a: No. Navy submarines are built to NAVSEA requirements; for NDT the key document is T9074-AS-GIB-010/271, and the limits a part must meet come from its drawing or order. Classification society rules are for commercial ships.

faq.q: We are an aerospace NDT supplier. Can our existing program be used for submarine work?
faq.a: Much of its structure and technical content usually carries over, but the written practice, recertification approach, surveillance records, vision standard and procedure qualification typically need rework for Navy-flowed orders. We map exactly what changes before you rewrite anything.

faq.q: What does the submarine safety boundary mean for a supplier's NDT?
faq.a: Items inside the boundary controlled by the Navy's submarine safety program carry stricter traceability and objective quality evidence requirements. Your purchase order identifies which items are affected and what evidence the prime expects with them.

faq.q: Who audits suppliers in the Groton supply chain?
faq.a: Mainly two parties: the prime contractor's supplier quality team, which approves you as a source, and the Navy's Supervisor of Shipbuilding, which inspects on the government's behalf. Either one may pull your NDT records.

faq.q: We are hiring many NDT trainees. What will an auditor check first?
faq.a: Whether each certified person's training hours, supervised experience, examinations and vision test are documented and dated before certification. Logs filled in after the fact are a common finding. See training records and certificates.

faq.q: Does Atlantis support work on submarine propulsion plants?
faq.a: No. Naval nuclear propulsion work and its quality regime are outside our scope. We support non-nuclear structure, tanks, piping, foundations, castings and outfitting.

faq.q: Will Atlantis radiograph our castings or welds?
faq.a: No. We do not perform radiography in the United States. A licensed radiography provider does that work, and our Level III can review its procedure and images for your file.

faq.q: Does Atlantis visit suppliers in Connecticut and Rhode Island?
faq.a: Yes, whenever the job needs someone on the shop floor, such as witnessing a qualification or running the rehearsal audit. There is no Atlantis office in New England, so the reading and drafting are done remotely.

faq.q: Is Atlantis approved by a class society?
faq.a: No. The approval is still in progress: we are in the process of obtaining it from ABS, Lloyd's Register and DNV, and until one of them issues a certificate we hold none.

faq.q: How should we answer an NDT finding from a prime's audit?
faq.a: State the cause, correct the specific item, describe the action that prevents recurrence, and attach dated evidence for each. Our audit documentation service helps prepare responses that close.
